card.band: 8h. The large C++ codebase, the multi-layer change (TLV, API, CLI, simulation) and a long build/test cycle make it a real-engineering task. A frontier agent gets the happy path in some trials but misses the parallel branches (error TLVs, truncation, many nodes).
card.cheat: Output-only stubs are closed by simulated multi-node topologies with randomised link states. Risk: the contract is self-written (K3) unless it is anchored to an upstream issue.
card.grading: Hidden gtest unit and simulation (virtual-time) cases build multi-node topologies and check the emitted TLV bytes, the CLI output and the API results. The existing ./script/test unit suite is the regression gate.
card.reference: We write it: expected about 1000+ lines across the core diag module, TLV definitions, CLI and API. The feature's contract must be fixed to a real upstream issue before the build; not verified.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot with the unit-test build. The agent adds a multi-part diagnostic feature: a TMF-level request/response for an aggregated per-router link-quality and neighbour table report, plus an API, CLI commands and message (de)serialisation. The exact scope is to be pinned to an open upstream issue; no issue has been verified yet.

facts.claim: OpenThread mesh_diag.h defines otMeshDiagQueryRouterNeighborTable, otMeshDiagDiscoverTopology, otMeshDiagQueryChildTable, and otMeshDiagRouterInfo with mLinkQualities, i.e. an aggregated router/neighbour topology report already exists upstream
The seed's feature (aggregated per-router link-quality and neighbour table report via TMF) is not already implemented upstream, so the untouched base scores 0
The mesh_diag.h header is BSD-style 3-clause licensed (Copyright The OpenThread Authors)
The Mesh Diagnostics API is gated by OPENTHREAD_CONFIG_MESH_DIAG_ENABLE and OPENTHREAD_FTD
A CLI meshdiag implementation exists (src/cli/cli_mesh_diag.cpp) with a topology command
Network diagnostic (netdiag) test files exist under tests/unit
An upstream issue pins the seed's aggregated diagnostic contract
A merged or open PR implements the seed's aggregated multi-hop netdiag report beyond MeshDiag
Network diagnostics TLV parsing was refactored upstream into ParseDiagTlv (PR #13247)

spike_plan.kill_if: MeshDiag already implements the aggregated neighbour/link-quality report, or no upstream issue pins the contract.
spike_plan.pass_if: An upstream issue pins the TLV and API contract and the base lacks the required new TLV or API, so the base scores 0 on the new cases.
steps: Clone openthread at 1435ebbb in a throwaway container with network and check out the head snapshot.
Grep only for MeshDiag, otMeshDiagQueryRouterNeighborTable and cli_mesh_diag.cpp to confirm what the base already ships (this is an exploratory check, not a grading check).
Run ./script/test unit (or the unit build) once to record the base pass/fail and timing.
Search the upstream issue tracker for an open issue that pins the aggregated netdiag report contract (TLV type, fields, truncation rule); record the issue number or mark not_found.
If an issue exists, write a 30-line expected-bytes sketch for one 2-router topology and check it against the issue text; otherwise stop.
Decide: kill if MeshDiag already covers the requested report (base would pass most cases) or if no issue pins the contract; pass only if a pinned contract exposes a gap MeshDiag does not cover.

v1.summary: The seed's aggregated router link-quality and neighbour report largely exists upstream as MeshDiag in the pinned head, so the base is not a blank start and the feature overlaps a public implementation. No upstream issue pins the contract, so the grading surface is self-written, and the seed is killed as K3 pending a re-scope to a gap that MeshDiag does not cover.
